title: Reconstruction is not decision identifiability: an exact collision for one-shot communication
description:
Scientific software and frozen reproducibility artifacts accompanying a study of the separation between model reconstructability, exact decision identifiability and local decision stability in one-shot communicated summaries.

The repository contains the frozen protocol chain for Phases 0-5, the feature-bank, pair and feature-map manifests, every gate summary, and the machine-readable artifacts behind the manuscript figures and supplementary analyses. It also contains a prospectively frozen cross-mechanism falsification study (CMR-V1) whose terminal decision was CMR-D with protocol stop; the later stages of that study were never run.

Raw third-party datasets, downloaded archives, local feature banks and pretrained model weights are not redistributed. Dataset access routes and model-weight provenance are documented in the repository README and in the per-phase manifests.

Known limitation. CMR-V1 has an incomplete source-level reproducibility status that is confined to that study: artefact internal consistency, CPU-CUDA numerical parity and decision-level determinism all pass, but the two source files that produced the frozen extraction run are not present at their recorded hashes. CMR-V1 is reported as a supplementary negative replication and is not used to broaden the manuscript's claim. The Phase 0-5 evidence chain carries its own protocol snapshots and artifact hashes and is unaffected.
